entries.description: **Write the missing Set 125 changelog fragment, then fold both targets.** Author `ai_router/changelog.d/` fragment for the read-only tool grant: what a routed call could do before (arbitrary shell, file create/edit, sub-agent spawning against the live working tree), what it can do now (`view`, `grep`, `glob`), and why it matters (a verifier able to edit the code it judges can report VERIFIED on its own edit). State it as the consumer-visible security-relevant change it is, not as a refactor. Then run `python -m ai_router.changelog fold --target router` and `--target extension` so the tagged commit carries real version sections rather than 16 loose fragments. **Do not invent entries for sets that already have fragments** — fold what is there; the gap being closed is Set 125 specifically. **Then make the breaking change self-remedying in the same pass.** The `1.0.0` section must state, at the top and in one screen: the symptom a user actually sees (config load refuses the spec), the one-line fix, and a working link to `docs/cross-repo-lightweight-removal-notice.md`. This replaces detection with remediation on purpose — it reaches every consumer of an open-source package, which no sweep of known checkouts can do.

**Rework the extension README into the Marketplace listing.** This is the pitch, and it is the artifact six staff and every future adopter read. Lead with what the framework *is* — the work is organized and standardized, and the verification is one you can check — not with what the AI writes. Use the new `media/ai-work-explorer.png` (committed in `d370e8f0`), referenced by **absolute raw.githubusercontent URL** like the existing image; a relative path does not render on the Marketplace. Also refresh `package.json`'s `description` and `keywords`, which are what Marketplace *search results* show and which are equally baked at publish. **Claim auditability, never efficacy.** Supported: the verifier is chosen by excluding the orchestrator's own provider (resolved from the model id, not a self-reported label); a session blocks rather than passing when no different-provider verifier exists; a close with no cross-provider evidence runs the verification itself; a finding closes only when its criterion fails before the fix and passes after; rounds are bounded and only the operator may authorize another; full suites run before commit, push and close. **Not supported and not to be claimed:** any defect-catch rate or "catches bugs before they ship" — the framework has never measured what fraction of real defects it finds. Keep the register of the existing docs (*"it is containment, not a sandbox, and the docs must not claim otherwise"*); that candour is the most credible asset here and a marketing pass must not sand it off.

**Correct the root README's two false statements.** It calls the tree "Session Set Explorer" (Set 132 S1 renamed it to **AI Work Explorer**, and `package.json` agrees; the stale phrase is line-wrapped, so grep for both halves). And its Prerequisites section states API-key accounts for all three providers are required — wrong for the Copilot-seat population that Sets 078/112 exist to serve, and wrong for the six staff now using it. Reconcile it with the seat path described earlier in the same file.
Required portion of the full test suite.

Wrote the Set 125 read-only tool grant fragment (Security), folded 17 router + 13 extension fragments, restructured both pending regions into the [1.0.0] / [0.51.0] version sections being tagged, and made the breaking change self-remedying at the top of 1.0.0 (symptom, one-line diff, working notice link). Restamped both baselines; round trip OK.

Reworked the extension README as the Marketplace listing: leads with what the framework is and that the verification is checkable, hero image swapped to media/ai-work-explorer.png by absolute raw.githubusercontent URL with descriptive alt text, added a 'Verification you can check' section carrying only the six supported auditability claims plus an explicit 'what this does not claim' block (no defect-catch rate) and the containment-not-a-sandbox register. Removed two false statements: the $0-budget 'or you skip verification' bullet (no skip exists post-1.0.0) and 'all three API keys are required'. Re-framed the 73/32% savings as the hypothetical Opus-baseline counterfactual the report actually computes. Refreshed package.json description + keywords.

Corrected both false statements in the root README: the activity-bar view is AI Work Explorer (Set 132 S1 rename, package.json agrees), and Prerequisites no longer requires API-key accounts for all three providers -- it now states the two answers (DIRECT_API with two of three keys as the working minimum, or a keyless COPILOT_CLI seat) and points at verify_type, reconciling with the seat path described earlier in the same file. RESIDUAL, out of scope by the spec's Non-goals: 'Session Set Explorer' survives in 25 other markdown files (most are dated proposals; the live ones are close-out.md, copilot-seat-setup-checklist.md, repository-reference.md, session-state-schema.md, spec-md-schema.md).

4 rounds, gpt-5-6-sol throughout, anthropic excluded as the orchestrator's effective provider via model-registry lookup. R1 discovery (2-way fan-out, spec-conformance + failure-scenario lenses): 1 Major -- the listing promised an unconditional cross-provider block while the same release documents an accepted same-provider fallback. R2 supplementary (harvest before remediating, per loop discipline): VERIFIED, 0 new. R3 remediation-review: REJECTED the fix -- package.json had been re-worded ('independent verification built into every close') rather than fixed, and the changelog argued the point instead of reporting it. R4 remediation-review: VERIFIED, fix accepted, 0 findings. Both rejections were correct and are recorded in the round-1 and round-3 remediation sidecars. Routed cost $2.5455.
